transcript.text: d/w not cleaning pls help, gritty bits left on glasses n bowls, beko

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Gritty bits on glasses usually mean water isn't reaching everything properly or isn't being filtered well enough during the wash. The most common causes for a Beko dishwasher are a clogged filter at the bottom of the tub or blocked spray-arm jets, but it can also be caused by items blocking the spray arms or using the wrong detergent cycle. Please check two things: 1. Remove the bottom rack and take out the filter at the base of the tub (twist and lift). Is it clogged with food or grit? 2. Spin the spray arms by hand—do they rotate freely, and are the small jet holes clear?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]

ok filter was full of food n grease, gross. upper spray arm is stiff to spin tho, lower one spins fine. holes on the upper one had some blocked with seeds n limescale, cleared them with a cocktail stick

Good work on clearing the debris. Since the lower arm spins fine but the upper one was stiff and had blockages, the remaining issue is likely that the upper arm's mounting point is still restricted by limescale or food residue, preventing it from spinning freely under pressure. Please check if the upper arm now spins smoothly by hand; if it still feels stiff or has wobble, that suggests a mechanical restriction on the arm itself rather than a pump fault.
[Helpful to see: image "Check and rinse the spray arm" — The spray arm spins to fire water through small jet holes. Check it spins freely and rinse the jets clear of food/grit. It usually unclips at the centre. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
upper one is still a bit stiff when i spin it by hand tbh, lower one is fine. what shud i do?

Since the arm is still stiff even after clearing the jets, the issue is probably restricted movement at its mounting point. Limescale or fine grit often builds up in the small bearing hole on the tub ceiling where the arm sits, acting like glue that stops it spinning freely under pressure. Please unclip the upper spray arm and check that mounting hole for scale buildup; if you find a ring of hard deposits, soaking the arm in hot water with descaler and cleaning the hole should free it up completely.
ok will try unclipping the upper arm n soak it. do i need anything special for the descaler or will normal kettle descaler do?

[Heading: Likely cause: spray arm bearing]
A standard kettle descaler will work perfectly fine for soaking the arm; just follow the bottle instructions. Once you've soaked it and cleaned out that mounting hole, try spinning the arm again—it should move freely now. To help me find the exact replacement part if this bearing is worn out, could you please tell me the model number of your dishwasher? It’s usually on a sticker on the side edge of the door frame.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
dont know the model number tbh, its a beko thats all. do i really need it? i was just going to clean the arm n see if it spins ok

[Heading: Likely cause: spray arm bearing]
No, you don't need the model number to fix it yourself. The stiffness is probably just a build-up of limescale in the mounting point, which soaking and cleaning will resolve.
